answer: Don't create the contractor by posting a bare record if you want NERM's normal processing (approvals, risk, notifications); the supported way is to start a Create workflow. For a direct insert, call POST https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com/api/profiles with header Authorization: Bearer <NERM API token> and Content-Type: application/json. Body: {"profiles":[{"profile_type_id":"<uuid of the Contractor profile type>","status":"Active","attributes":{"personal_first_name":"Ada","personal_last_name":"Lovelace","email":"ada@vendor.com","start_date":"2026-12-01","end_date":"2027-06-30","organization":"<uuid of the Vendor profile>"}}]}. The attribute keys must be the attribute uids defined in Admin > Attributes. Reference attributes (vendor/organization, manager) take the UUID of the target profile or user. Get profile_type_id from GET /api/profile_types. To create through a workflow, use POST /api/workflow_sessions with workflow_id, requester_id and requester_type, plus the attributes.

NERM is a separate SaaS that lives at https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com, and its API has its own authentication. An ISC personal access token, or an ISC OAuth client_credentials token, will not work against /api. In NERM, create an API user/token: Admin > Settings (Advanced) > API Users / API Tokens. Pick the scopes, then copy the token, which is shown only once. Send it on every call as Authorization: Bearer <token>, with Accept: application/json and Content-Type: application/json. Tokens are long-lived bearer secrets, so store them in a vault and rotate them. Use one token per integration with least-privilege scopes. Calls without a valid token return 401, and calls with insufficient scope return 403. ISC credentials only come into play the other way round, in the ISC NERM source/connector configuration, where ISC calls NERM with the NERM token.

Give the token only the scopes it needs. That means profile read (profiles:read, or 'Read' on Profiles) and workflow-session create (workflow_sessions:create, or 'Create' on Workflow Sessions). Do not grant write/update/delete on profiles, users, or admin objects. If the workflow reads profile types or workflows to resolve ids, add read on profile_types and workflows too. Scopes are fixed when the API token is created in NERM Admin > API. You usually cannot edit them in place, so you create a new token and revoke the old one. If a scope is missing, NERM rejects the call with HTTP 403 Forbidden (or 401 with an 'unauthorized/insufficient scope' message). Nothing is partially executed. Your integration should log the 403 and treat it as a configuration error, not something to retry.

Use offset/limit paging on GET https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com/api/profiles?limit=500&offset=0. Increase offset by limit until a page comes back with fewer than limit records or an empty profiles array. 500 is the practical maximum page size, which means about 400 calls for 200k profiles. Add filters to reduce volume, for example profile_type_id=<uuid> or status, and request only the attributes you need. Deep offsets get slow and are unstable if data changes during the run. So sort deterministically (order by id or created_at), and preferably run an incremental export using updated_at, or the 'after' / last-id cursor where it is available, instead of a full dump every night. Respect rate limits: on HTTP 429, back off and honour Retry-After. Parallelise moderately, partitioned by profile type. Write each page to staging and checkpoint the offset so a failed run can resume.

POST /api/workflow_sessions only creates the session. Whether it runs depends on the workflow type and the payload. Common causes: (1) The workflow is a Create/Update request workflow whose first step is a form or request step that waits for human input, so it sits pending in the requester's/approver's queue. (2) It is waiting on an approval step, so check the approver's inbox. (3) You didn't supply required attributes or the profile reference (profile_id/uid for update workflows), so the step can't complete. (4) The workflow is inactive or the wrong workflow_id was used. (5) requester_id/requester_type (e.g. NeprofileUser) is invalid. Check GET /api/workflow_sessions/{id} and its status/current step in the UI under Workflows > Sessions. Use an Automated workflow, or provide all attributes in the body ("attributes":{...}), so that steps with no user interaction auto-advance.

Use the profile search/advanced query endpoint rather than a plain GET with query string filters. POST https://{tenant}.nonemployee.com/api/advanced_search/run (or the profiles query endpoint). Body example: {"advanced_search":{"condition_rules_attributes":[{"type":"ProfileTypeRule","comparison_operator":"==","value":"<profile_type_id>"},{"type":"ProfileAttributeRule","condition_object_id":"<attribute id of personal_first_name>","object_type":"NeAttribute","comparison_operator":"starts_with","value":"a"},{"type":"ProfileStatusRule","comparison_operator":"!=","value":"Terminated"}]}} with limit/offset for paging. A simpler alternative is to GET /api/profiles?status=Active (also add OnLeave/Pending if you need them) and filter first names client-side, case-insensitively, since the match may be case-sensitive. Remember that 'non-terminated' includes Active, Inactive, On Leave and Pending.

SailPoint NERM (Non-Employee Risk Management, from the SecZetta acquisition) is a separate product on its own tenant ({tenant}.nonemployee.com). It is a full system of record for third parties. It has configurable profile types (people and non-people: vendors, assets, devices), relationships between profiles, multi-step workflows (create/update/automated, approvals, vendor-portal/delegated collaboration, REST API steps), risk scoring, attestations/reviews, and its own REST API. It integrates with ISC through a NERM source/connector. ISC Non-Employee Lifecycle Management (NELM) is a lighter feature built into ISC. You define Non-Employee sources with up to 50 sources and a fixed attribute schema plus a few custom ones. Records are created manually, by CSV upload, or via the /non-employee-records API, with simple approval flows. Those records become identities through aggregation. There are no risk scores, no organisation/vendor portals, and no complex workflows. Choose NELM for simple contractor onboarding and NERM for heavy third-party risk and vendor management.

In NERM, risk is defined on attributes. Admins mark attributes as risk-relevant and assign a risk score/weight to each possible value, for example citizenship, background-check result, access to sensitive data, or location. Typically these are selection-type attributes (single/multi select, checkbox, radio), but the profile's risk level can also be set by a workflow. A profile's overall risk score is computed from the risk values of its scored attributes. Each attribute contributes its value's score times the attribute weight, and the result is normalised to the configured scale and mapped to risk levels (Low/Medium/High/Critical) through thresholds set per profile type. Risk can also roll up through relationships, so a person inherits part of the risk of their vendor/organisation profile. The score recalculates whenever a scored attribute changes. It is exposed on the profile (risk_score/risk_level) and can drive workflow conditions, reviews and ISC policies via sync.

Use the SailPoint NERM source in ISC, configured with the NERM tenant URL and an API token. The account identity/correlation attribute is the NERM profile id (uid), typically correlated to an ISC identity attribute through the email or an employee/uid attribute in the correlation config. Usually you correlate on profile id for the native identity and on email for identity correlation. Only profiles of the profile types selected in the source configuration get aggregated, normally the people types such as Contractor, not vendors or assets. Often only certain statuses are included (exclude Terminated if filtered). Not all attributes sync. Only attributes mapped in the NERM source account schema / attribute mapping come across: standard name/email/status/manager plus the attributes you add. Reference attributes arrive as ids or names. ISC can also push attributes back (writeback) only for mapped fields. Run full aggregation on a schedule and use NERM-triggered events for near-real-time updates.

Yes, there are two problems. (1) Order: setting Status to Terminated before the manager approval means the profile is terminated and, via the ISC sync, access is deprovisioned before anyone approves. If the manager rejects, you have to reverse it manually. Put the approval step first, then branch on its outcome, then do the Status Change. Also note that a terminated profile may fall out of scope for later steps and notifications. (2) The REST API step is synchronous with a timeout of roughly 30 seconds. A slow service can time out and fail the step, which stops or errors the workflow session. Make the downstream call asynchronous: have the service accept the request and return 200/202 quickly, then do the work and call back into the NERM API, for example by updating the profile or starting another workflow session. Also configure error handling or a failure branch, and keep the step idempotent in case it is retried.
